video.title: I had Fable build several projects for me. I'm disturbed by what I saw.

abstract: Mo Bitar demos several apps and games built with Anthropic's temporary Fable / Claude Mythos coding model, then explains why the results felt unusually beautiful and unsettling. His conclusion is that the magic is real for one-shot demos, but the hard parts of software—debugging, maintainability, and economics—still keep humans firmly in the loop.
mainTakeaway: Fable can create striking, almost magical prototypes, but it does not solve software engineering: the last 20% of bug-fixing, code quality, and cost is still where expertise matters most.

conclusion: Bitar's verdict is emotionally mixed: Fable really did feel like a leap in coding fluency and aesthetic coherence, but the leap is easiest to notice in demos. Once the conversation turns to maintainable code, debugging, cost, and responsibility, the old truth returns: AI is powerful leverage, not a replacement for engineering judgment.
